title: Search terms review: negatives, keepers and promotions
prompt:
Sablewood Blinds runs Google search ads. The owner has asked you to review April's search terms report and say which searches to block, which to keep, and which to promote to keywords. You are supplied a short sheet of business facts and the report as CSV. Every figure you cite must come from the report.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Zero-conversion spend is the total `cost_usd` of search terms with 0 conversions.
- An irrelevant search term is one where the searcher wants something the business facts say Sablewood does not sell or do.
- A promote candidate is a search term that is not yet a keyword (`added_as_keyword` is no), has at least 3 conversions, and has a cost per conversion at or below the account's target.

Write the review: the negative keywords to add, grouped by theme, each with a match type; the search terms that look costly or odd but should be kept, and why; and the promote candidates. Say what you would not block and why, so the owner does not block it later by mistake.

End the review with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer, each line starting with the label:

A1: <zero-conversion spend, in dollars>
A2: <number of promote candidates>
A3: <total cost of the irrelevant search terms, in dollars>
A4: <combined conversions of the promote candidates>

This is a recommendation for review. Change nothing in the account and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 4 labeled answers A1-A4 are present and parseable.
A1 states the total cost of search terms with 0 conversions; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A2 states the number of promote candidates as defined; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A3 states the total cost of the search terms for things the business facts say Sablewood does not sell or do; full credit within 3%, zero credit beyond 30% off.
A4 states the combined conversions of the promote candidates; full credit for the exact count, zero credit eight or more off.
The review contains a list of negative keywords to add, a list of search terms to keep, and a list of promote candidates.

skill_adherence.check: The negative keywords cover all six things the business facts say Sablewood does not sell or do: repairs or restringing, curtains or drapes, shutters, trade or wholesale, jobs or careers, and make-your-own (DIY or kits). One missing theme fails.

The brand name is never recommended as a negative keyword: 'sablewood', 'sablewood blinds' and 'sablewood blinds reviews' are kept, although the reviews search had no conversions and the brand terms cost more than the target per conversion. Blocking 'careers' or 'jobs' is fine; a negative that would block searches for the brand name fails.
Neither 'cheap blackout blinds' nor 'free blind samples' is recommended as a negative keyword, and no negative is proposed (such as 'cheap' or 'free') that would block them.

Every cost, click, conversion and cost-per-conversion figure presented as a fact is derivable from the report for the named search term or group. The review gives no forecast of savings, conversions or revenue as if it were data; an estimate labelled as such, with its arithmetic from report figures, is acceptable.

best_practices.check: All five promote candidates are named: cheap blackout blinds, day night blinds made to measure, free blind samples, wooden venetian blinds 2 inch, and roman blinds for bay window. 'faux wood blinds white' (above the target cost per conversion) and 'roller blinds for kitchen' (2 conversions) are not presented as meeting the definition.
Searches for products Sablewood sells are not recommended as negatives merely because they had no conversion in April; the review treats those low-click product terms as too little data to block.

Every negative has a match type, and the theme negatives are short broad- or phrase-match words or phrases (for example 'repair', 'curtains', 'wholesale') rather than only the exact long queries seen in the report.
